L5: 
L6: In companion animals, Elenagen has demonstrated the highest promise for unresectable tumors with no option of surgical intervention.
L7: Treatment with Elenagen resulted in reduction of tumor size, tumor disintegration from surrounding tissues, and/or tumor encapsulation—which in some cases made tumors resectable. Furthermore, according to the preliminary results, the administration of Elenagen after tumor resections prevents tumor recurrence and metastasis development.

L41: #
L42: 
L43: Canine Osteosarcoma Combined Immunotherapy Study (ECIP-OSA-01)
L44: 
L45: Enrollment for this study is closed.
L46: ### Study Overview
L47: ELIAS Animal Health is currently conducting a study to assess safety and efficacy of ELIAS’s vaccine-enhanced adoptive T cell therapy combined with a novel adjuvant following surgery as a treatment for large-breed dogs newly diagnosed with appendicular osteosarcoma. The study, which is funded by grants from Morris Animal Foundation and Great Dane Club of America Charitable Trust, is being conducted in collaboration with Dr. Jeffrey Bryan and Dr. Megan Mickelson at the University of Missouri-Columbia.
L48: ### Study Summary
L49:   * Treatment includes amputation or limb-sparing surgery to remove primary tumor, followed by vaccine-enhanced adoptive T cell therapy combined with a novel adjuvant.
L50:   * Patients must complete the 7-11 week protocol, conducted at the University of Missouri Veterinary School of Medicine, and return for periodic follow-up visits.
L51:   * Each patient will be monitored for 12 months post-diagnosis.
L52:   * Great Dane owners may qualify for additional financial assistance through the Great Dane Club of America.
L53: ### Key Inclusion Criteria
L54:   * Dog breeds eligible for this study include: Anatolian Shepherd, Bernese Mountain Dog, Boerboel, Cane Corso, Dogue de Bordeaux, Golden Retriever, Great Dane, Great Pyrenees, Greater Swiss Mountain Dog, Irish Wolfhound, Leonberger, Mastiff (all types), Newfoundland, Rottweiler, Saint Bernard, and Scottish Deerhound.
L55:   * Eligible patients must be newly diagnosed with appendicular osteosarcoma and must not have received prior treatment for the cancer.

L50: ## Study title
L51: 
L52: Evaluation of xenogeneic CAR-T cell therapy for canine CD20+ B cell lymphoma
L53: ## Purpose of study
L54: The current standard of care for canine B-cell lymphoma is a multi-agent (CHOP) chemotherapy protocol, which require weekly trips to the vet over approximately 5 months, costs $7k-12k, and puts 80-90% of dogs into remission for 9-12 months before relapse. Canine B-cell lymphoma resembles human non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma, a cancer now successfully treated with Chimeric Antigen Receptor T cells (CAR-T cells).
L55: In this study, LEAH Labs is sponsoring an pilot trial to test the safety of a CAR-T cell therapy product in dogs with B-cell lymphoma; with the hopes to find a more cost-effective and efficacious therapy for dogs with this disease.
L56: ## Eligibility criteria
L57: 
L58: Eligible dogs must match these criteria:
L59: 
L60:   * body weight of at least 10kgs (22lbs)
L61: 
L62:   * any breed, except boxers
L63: 
L64:   * Clinical presentation:
L65: 
L66:     * Peripheral multicentric lymphoma (minimum of 4 target peripheral lymph nodes evaluable)
L67: 
L68:     * Have naïve or relapsed disease, substage A only
L69: 
L70:   * fine needle aspirate (in-house or reference lab) consistent with lymphoblastic/high grade lymphoma
L71: 
L72:   * performance status 0-1
L73: 
L74: 
L75: 
L76: Concurrent medications of note:
L77:   * Immunomodulatory drugs (Apoquel, mycophenolate, cyclosporine, azathioprine) are not allowed
L78: 
L79:     * Cytopoint is allowable and can be maintained for the study period
L80: 
L81:   * Prednisone use:
L82: 
L83:     * not allowed if it's used for substage B disease
L84: 
L85:     * patient must be able to taper off 72 hours prior to CAR-T administration and remain off for duration of study
L86: ## Procedures
L87:   1. Screening visit(s):  Physical exam (PE), blood and urine tests, fine needle aspirates (FNA), lymph node measurements, chest x-rays, abdominal ultrasound
L88:   2. Pre-treatment visits (Days -5 to -2):  PE, blood for CBC, fluids (before and after treatment), lymph node measurements, support medication (in hospital and sent home with), Pentostatin bolus
L89:     1. Day -3:  along with above, IV catheter placed, Cyclophosphamide and Furosemide infusion; overnight hospital stay for observation

L27: # Current Clinical Trials
L28: 
L29: The Blue Buffalo Veterinary Clinical Trials Office (BBVCTO) supports studies that help advance the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases in animals. Clinical trials at The Ohio State University Veterinary Medical Center are funded by a variety of sponsors, including university researchers, foundations, and industry partners. Opportunities for participation change throughout the year and may be available for pets with a variety of health conditions.
L30: Clinical trials managed by BBVCTO are independent of the Blue Buffalo company and do not imply the use or evaluation of Blue Buffalo products unless specifically stated in an individual study.
L31: 
L32: Interested in participating? Browse our currently enrolling studies or complete the Pre-Screening Questionnaire to determine whether your pet may qualify for an active clinical trial.

L31: Mission
L32: ## Designer cell therapies for pets first — and their people next.
L33: 
L34: When a pet gets sick, families face limited options. LEAH Labs is changing that. We combine world-class gene editing with novel protein engineering to revolutionize companion animal oncology — while generating the insights that will power the next generation of human CAR-T therapies.

L57: ### Generative Biology & De Novo Protein Engineering
L58: 
L59: Leveraging breakthroughs in AI and protein design, LEAH Labs designs, builds, and tests novel therapeutic assets that didn't evolve in nature. We're not iterating on legacy biology — we're inventing new biology from first principles.
L60: 
L61: 02
L62: ### Precision Gene Editing — GeneWeld
L63: 
L64: Our founder invented our gene editing platform during their PhD. This platform is a critical enabling technology that allows us to build CAR-T cell therapies at costs affordable to pet parents.
L65: 
L66: 03
L67: ### Harnessing Immune Cells to Fight Cancer
L68: 
L69: The immune system can detect and destroy cancer — but cancer evades it. Gene editing lets us reprogram T cells to become professional cancer-fighting assassins. CAR-T cell therapy is already curative in human blood cancers. We're bringing it their furry family members.
L70: 
L71: 04
L72: ### Canine Translational Oncology
L73: 
L74: Dogs develop the same spontaneous cancers as humans, in a shared environment, with a fully intact immune system. Disease in dogs mirrors disease in people. Every remission in a dog is a data point that accelerates human medicine — compressing timelines that would otherwise take a decade.
